fields.title: Reestr: registrations tripled, paid users stayed flat
fields.summary: A quarter of traffic growth brought no paid users. Decide where to focus the next quarter.
fields.decisionPrompt: Where will you direct the next quarter and why?
fields.brief/role: You are the product manager at Reestr.
fields.brief/company: Reestr is a fictional document management service for small business: invoices, acts, signatures. 1 200 ₽ monthly subscription, 14-day trial.
fields.brief/context: Over the quarter, Marketing tripled registrations. Paid users grew by only 6%. The budget for next quarter is the same; leadership expects an explanation and a plan.
fields.brief/objective: Decide what to focus on in the next quarter.
fields.brief/constraints: Quarterly budget is 900 thousand, one marketer, engineering allocates two developers for half-time.
fields.brief/task: Choose what to do and justify it.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: A cheap lead and a cheap paying customer are different things
fields.learnTakeaway/body: A channel is evaluated by customer acquisition cost and payback period; everything higher up the funnel is intermediate numbers that are easy to fool yourself with. When the funnel drops, choose the step not by the worst percentage, but by segment breakdown: often a bad step is bad for only one acquisition source, and the real fix is to stop acquiring people who don't need the product.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content:
Social media, targeting 'business owners': 620 thousand ₽, 2 950 registrations (210 ₽), 89 paying. CAC 6 966 ₽.

Search for queries like 'how to invoice an IP': 210 thousand ₽, 620 registrations (339 ₽), 131 paying. CAC 1 603 ₽.

Partnership with accounting service: no budget, 40 registrations, 22 paying.

Organic and recommendations: 310 registrations, 58 paying.

Average check 1 200 ₽/mo. Paying users stay 14 months on average, LTV ≈ 16 800 ₽.

75% of the quarterly budget went to social media: leads are cheaper there.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content:
Overall: visit → registration 9% → first document 38% → payment 22%.

First document creation by channel:
Search — 61%;
Social media — 14%;
Partnerships — 72%.

Payment conversion after first document is roughly equal across channels: 21–24%.

Between registration and first document, a user goes through: email confirmation, entering company details (11 fields), selecting a template.

There is no 'looked at pricing and left' step in analytics — people visit the pricing page, but further events are untracked.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content:
Paid user retention at 30 days: 71%. At 90 days: 58%.

Among users who invited an accountant during the first week, 84% stay after 90 days. 6% invite an accountant.

Among those who created three or more documents in week one — 79% stay. This segment is 19%.

Task frequency: invoices are issued 2–4 times a month, acts are closed at month-end.

Last quarter launched a daily email digest: 4% open rate, 12% unsubscribed. Never touched again.

Churn reason (cancellation survey): 'don't use it' — 44%, 'too expensive' — 21%, 'lacks features' — 18%.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content:
Two main competitors: a large enterprise document system (3x price, 2-week implementation, has everything) and a budget service for 400 ₽ (invoices only, no signatures).

Reestr's website says: 'Modern document management service. Convenient, fast, reliable.'

In 12 interviews with paid users asked why Reestr is better, nine gave the same answer: 'I issued my first invoice in five minutes without asking anyone to set it up.'

Sales complains that prospects compare them to the budget service and ask for discounts.

Users get a 14-day trial; 63% of registrations do not create a single document during trial.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Reallocate budget by channel unit economics and fix first document flow
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Shift budget based on customer acquisition cost rather than lead cost, and fix the step from registration to first document where channels diverge.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence:
Calculating by paying users flips the picture: social media gives a CAC of 6 966 ₽ with an LTV of 16 800 ₽ and pays back in 5.8 months; search gives 1 603 ₽ and one and a half months. You reallocate the budget to search and partnerships, knowing that search capacity is limited and needs to be measured.
Next, the first document: you reduce 11 credential fields to three with auto-fill by TIN, setting the template by default. The share of those creating their first document grows from 38% to 52%.
You add an accountant invite to onboarding—the share grows from 6% to 21%, with retention in this group at 63%: lower than 84%, meaning part of the previous effect was selection, and you record this honestly.
In a quarter, paying users are +71% on the same budget, with portfolio payback at 2.4 months.
Trade-off: total registrations drop nearly in half, and you had to explain this to leadership separately.
fields.decisionOptions/1/label: Scale the channel with the cheapest lead
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Social media yields signups at 210 ₽ vs 339 ₽ in search. Increase budget there to get even more signups.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence:
Registrations grow by another one and a half times, and the report looks great.
Paying users increase by 27 people with 400 thousand in extra budget: CAC for this growth is around 14 800 ₽ with an LTV of 16 800 ₽.
Payback stretches beyond a year, leaving no money for the next quarter.
Support gets a flood of registrations that create nothing: 86% from social media never reach their first document.
By the end of the quarter, management asks the same question as at the start, only harsher.
Trade-off: the channel was evaluated by entry price rather than result price—the same mistake that led to the current situation.
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Only 58% stay after 90 days. Set up regular notifications and emails to bring users back more often.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence:
Past experience repeats: daily email digest had 4% open rate and 12% unsubscribes; new email series behaves similarly.
One email works — a reminder on the 25th about unsigned acts: 47% open, 31% return. It aligns with when the natural need arises.
90-day retention improves slightly from 58% to 62%.
Main drop-off untouched: 63% of signups never create a single document, and 44% of churn says 'don't use it' — these people never started using the product.
Trade-off: effort spent on existing paying users while losing the vast majority before payment.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Offer 50% discount for the first month
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: 21% of churn cite 'too expensive', Sales asks for discounts. Lower entry barrier to get more payments.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence:
First-month paid conversions increase by 34% — numbers look like a win.
In month two, only 41% stay at full price: users were buying the discount, not the product.
Cohort LTV drops to 9 400 ₽; with social media CAC at 6 966 ₽, payback deteriorates.
Sales now asks for discounts on every deal, including those that previously paid full price.
Meanwhile, 'don't use it' — 44% of churn — remains unaddressed.
Trade-off: price cut where price wasn't the main problem, making it hard to restore standard pricing.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Channel chosen by popularity rather than intent and testable bet
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Acquisition cost evaluated by leads, without conversion to payment or payback
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Bottleneck identified by lowest percentage rather than highest leverage
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Failed to find the action after which churn stops
fields.rubric/remediation/4/gap: Retention mechanic does not match the natural frequency of the task
fields.rubric/remediation/5/gap: Differentiation defined as 'better at everything', which means nothing
